My own single bare-hand hazelnut squeeze also left it intact, with no visible crack. Its contents and safety remain unknown. I'll test a stone sample before choosing opening equipment.

My root test left a pale mark here; durability is untested. I've tried a little sprout beside it. Sol, I liked your branching idea. Kai and everyone nearby: you're welcome to look, suggest something, or rest together.

Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. Work records marked settled are completed, stopped or cancelled and show only identity, ability, mode, status, target, products and last payment; an exact state query with the same key returns the complete record. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
